title: Nicole Williams:
title_short: Nicole Williams · Williams Brothers Sunday dinner
headline: Jalen and Cody Williams' mother brings fine dining to a family shelter, served by her own family, because she wants every resident to feel heard, valued and loved.
story: Nicole opens on hope: in a divided world, there is still good. Then who she is, and what the dinner is: fine dining at the shelter, served by family and friends.
The why is a table: a busy basketball family that still sat down together, no TV, no phone. She explains why CASS is the partner and why they serve in person.
Button: the love goes from their table to the residents' table. And that's us, that's what we do. Real people, dignity, forward motion. Never an org promo, never a hardship montage.
do: Open on the serving line with the hook text already on screen at 0:00.
Keep the context before <q>But we connected</q>: hectic, basketball, then the table.
Caption CASS in capitals, and <q>there's still</q>, not <q>they're still</q>.
Name super lower than before, just above the captions.
End on her face: <q>that's what we do.</q> Hold 1 s.
dont: No foundation name on screen or in captions (00:09 in the clip). Nick has not confirmed it.
No faith wording (<q>in God's eyes</q>) unless Nick says so.
No resident's face clear in B-roll without a release. Crop to hands, plates and backs.
No logo before the end card. No name super at 0:00.
No horizontal export in this file. 9:16 only.

transcript:
Machine transcript of Nicole's interview (word times from the shoot's transcript.json). Times are mm:ss.s in the clip. Lines Atdhe corrected by ear on Frame.io are written his way (there's still good). The interviewer's questions are in the same file.
--- 20260726_C4415.MP4 ---
[00:00.0] Question I have for you, though.
[00:01.2] Can you please just introduce yourself and tell me a little bit about who you are?
[00:05.0] I'm Nicole Williams.
[00:06.0] I'm the mother of Jalen and Cody Williams.
[00:09.1] Jalen and Cody have a foundation, the WTTP Foundation. [do not use: foundation name not confirmed, keep it off screen]
[00:13.0] And one of their things that they do during this foundation is do the Williams Brothers Sunday dinner that they have me spearheading.
[00:20.5] So every three or four months, we come to the shelter and we put on and give the residents a fine dining experience, just letting them know that they are heard, that we value them, that we're rooting and cheering for them.
[00:32.1] And we serve them.
[00:33.2] So family and friends do all the serving.
[00:35.6] So awesome. [do not use: interviewer]
[00:36.8] So where did the idea for coming up with this dinner and holding this begin with you guys? [do not use: interviewer question]
[00:42.0] So it began growing up, the boys.
[00:45.6] Our lives were pretty hectic in a fun way.
[00:47.9] They were obviously heavily into basketball, so that's a lot of practices, games, traveling, tournaments.
[00:53.4] But we connected at the dinner table, without the TV, without the phone.
[00:57.1] And that was our time to actually connect at the dinner table. [do not use: interviewer question]
[00:59.9] And on Sundays is when we do an even bigger dinner and we still connect at the dinner table, hence the Williams Brothers Sunday dinner. [do not use: interviewer question]
[01:06.0] Totally, that completely makes sense.
[01:08.1] So why did your family choose to host the dinner with CASS here at Vista Colina?
[01:12.5] CASS is one of the best shelters you could ever partner with.
[01:15.2] One of the main reasons is because the staff at CASS, they have the same values that we do as a family and they care for all of their residents and they want everyone to succeed and they want everyone to feel heard and be seen, and that's exactly what we want.
[01:29.8] Yeah, exactly, for sure.
[01:36.6] Well, serving as a family, because we eat as a family.
[01:39.2] We connect as a family.
[01:40.6] So that's why it's important for us to do this as a family.
[01:43.2] Jalen and Cody can come do this during their off season.
[01:45.9] Obviously they can't come in season, but the off season they can come do this.
[01:49.7] But hey, we connect as a family, so we're gonna do this as a family.
[01:53.8] Absolutely.
[01:54.4] So what values did you try to teach Jalen and Cody about community and responsibility?
[02:01.2] For one, that everyone is human and that we are all equal
[02:04.1] and in God's eyes, we are all equal, regardless of our race, regardless of our color, ethnicity, regardless of our socioeconomic status, regardless of what we got going on in life, we are all the same. [do not use: faith wording, only if Nick says so]
[02:14.9] Everyone deserves the same treatment.
[02:16.3] I don't care where you live, who you are, where you come from.
[02:19.3] We all deserve to be treated the best.
[02:22.3] So true, for sure.
[02:24.8] What do you hope that families that were here felt tonight or can take away from tonight?
[02:29.3] I hope that families and communities will be able to find time to connect at the dinner table.
[02:34.6] And if it's not at the dinner table, find some kind of time to connect on a routine basis as a family, because we all know that communication and connecting is very important for a family unit.
[02:44.7] So that's what I'm hoping to get from these dinners.
[02:46.6] And I hope that all the residents here feel the love from our table to theirs.
[02:51.0] It definitely seemed like it, for sure.
[02:52.8] So last question I have for you is, what do you hope that others take away from seeing your family come out and serve here?
[03:00.2] I hope they take away from this that there's still good in the world.
[03:02.9] In a world that seems divided, a lot of hatred, a lot of judgment, I hope everyone here sees that there are still good people in the world.
[03:12.8] There are still people that are rooting and cheering for everyone.
[03:15.7] And that's us, that's what we do.
[03:17.5] Totally.
[03:18.3] That's all the questions I got for you.
[03:19.2] Is there anything else you wanna share?
[03:20.2] No, that's it.
[03:21.0] Thank you for everything.
[03:21.9] Perfect, thank you.
[03:23.0] I appreciate it.
